sections.title: Orthogonal complements and the matrix transpose

variables.meaning: a vector whose dot product with w is formed: v = [3, 2] of Figure 6.1.4, whose length is √13, and the v of Figure 6.1.8, compared with u and w for similarity
the other factor of the dot product v·w and the other arm of the angle θ between v and w; in Preview Activity 6.1.1, the rotation of v by 90°, orthogonal to v
the third of the three vectors u, v, w of Figure 6.1.8, which appears rather dissimilar to both v and w
the vector x = [−2, 3] of Activity 6.1.2, perpendicular to v = [3, 2]; a general vector [x, y, z] in the exercises
the components v₁, v₂, …, v_m of the vector v, multiplied by the components of w in the dot product v·w = v₁w₁ + v₂w₂ + … + v_mw_m
the components w₁, w₂, …, w_m of the vector w
the angle between the vectors v and w, which the dot product measures: v·w = |v||w| cos θ
a scalar multiplying a vector or a matrix, as in (sv)·w = s(v·w) and (sA)ᵀ = sAᵀ

the weights c₁, c₂ of a linear combination c₁v₁ + c₂v₂ in the distributive property of the dot product; in k-means clustering, the centers c₁, c₂, …, c_k of the clusters, each updated to the centroid of its cluster
the first of the vectors v₁, v₂ of a linear combination dotted with w; in k-means clustering, the first of the data points v₁, v₂, …, vₙ viewed as vectors, v₁ = [−2, 1] in Activity 6.1.4
the second of the vectors v₁, v₂ dotted with w; the second data point, v₂ = [1, 1] in Activity 6.1.4
the third data point of Activity 6.1.4, v₃ = [1, 2]
the fourth data point of Activity 6.1.4, v₄ = [3, 2]
the dimension of a vector, the number of its components; the number of rows of an m × n matrix, which is the dimension of its columns and of the product Ax
the number of vectors v₁, v₂, …, vₙ whose centroid (1/n)(v₁ + v₂ + … + vₙ) is formed
the number of clusters into which the data points are grouped, chosen at the elbow of the objective; also the unknown component of the vector [6, k] of Activity 6.1.2
the centroid of a set of vectors, c = [3, 2] for [1, 1], [4, 1], [4, 4]
the clusters C₁, C₂, …, C_k of a clustering, C₁ the set of data points closest to the center c₁
the first unknown of a linear equation in two or three unknowns, the first coordinate of a point (x, y) or (x, y, z)
the second unknown of a linear equation in two or three unknowns, the second coordinate of a point (x, y) or (x, y, z)
a time series, a vector whose components record a quantity over time, such as a company's stock value on consecutive days (Activity 6.1.3)
the first of the stock time series s₁ (blue) and s₂ (orange) of Activity 6.1.3, which rise and fall in roughly similar ways; their correlation is 0.98
the second of the stock time series s₁ and s₂ of Activity 6.1.3
a third time series of Activity 6.1.3, whose correlation with s₁ is −0.87
a fourth time series of Activity 6.1.3, whose correlation with s₁ is −0.10
the demeaned time series s̃₁, obtained from s₁ by subtracting its average value; the correlation of s₁ and s₂ is the cosine of the angle between s̃₁ and s̃₂
the demeaned time series s̃₂, obtained from s₂ by subtracting its average value
the first of two time series t₁, t₂ whose demeaned series are scalar multiples of one another, as in Figure 6.1.9
the second of the time series t₁, t₂ of Figure 6.1.9, whose demeaned series is a positive or a negative multiple of t̃₁
the demeaned series of t₁
the demeaned series of t₂, a scalar multiple of t̃₁, so that the correlation of t₁ and t₂ is 1 or −1
a vector n perpendicular to a line, so that n·(x − p) = 0 for every point x on the line; n = [1, 2] in Figure 6.1.16, and n = [A, B] for the line Ax + By = C (Exercise 6.1.11)
a point p on a line, p = [2, 2] in Figure 6.1.16, with n·x = n·p for every point x of the line (Exercise 6.1.11)
a vector whose orthogonal complement is sought: v = [−1, 2] in Preview Activity 6.2.1, and v = [1, −2, 3], which defines the line L of Example 6.2.4
a general vector x required to be orthogonal to the basis vectors of W, the unknown of the system Bx = 0 or Aᵀx = 0 whose solution set is W⊥
the components x₁, x₂, …, xₙ of the vector x, the unknowns of the linear system Ax = b and the weights of the linear combination of the columns of A
a vector w = c₁w₁ + c₂w₂ in the subspace W, a linear combination of its basis; the vector w = [−2, 2, 3] dotted with the columns of A in Activity 6.2.3
the first of the vectors w₁, w₂, …, wₙ forming a basis for the subspace W, a column of the matrix A = [w₁ w₂ … wₙ]; w₁ = [1, 0, −2] in Activity 6.2.2
the second basis vector of W, the second column of A; w₂ = [1, 1, −1] in Activity 6.2.2
the last of the basis vectors w₁, w₂, …, wₙ of the n-dimensional subspace W, the last column of A
the first of the columns v₁, v₂, …, vₙ of A, whose dot products with x are the components of Aᵀx; in Example 6.2.5 and Activity 6.2.5, the first basis vector of W⊥
the second column of A; the second basis vector of W⊥
the third basis vector of W⊥ in Example 6.2.5, v₃ = [−2, 0, 1, 0, 1]
the last of the columns v₁, v₂, …, vₙ of A in Proposition 6.2.8
a line through the origin, the set of scalar multiples of a vector, a 1-dimensional subspace
the orthogonal complement of the line L, the set of vectors orthogonal to every vector on L: a line in ℝ² or a plane in ℝ³
a subspace of ℝᵐ, such as a line or a plane through the origin, whose orthogonal complement W⊥ and orthogonal projections onto it are formed; W = Col(A) when its basis vectors are the columns of A
the orthogonal complement of W, the set of vectors in ℝᵐ each of which is orthogonal to every vector in W; a subspace with dim W⊥ = m − dim W, and Nul(Aᵀ) when W = Col(A)
the matrix A = [w₁ w₂ … wₙ] whose columns form a basis of W, so that W = Col(A) and W⊥ = Nul(Aᵀ); the 2 × 4 matrix of Example 6.2.7 whose transpose is formed
the transpose of the m × n matrix A, the n × m matrix whose rows are the columns of A; the components of Aᵀx are the dot products of the columns of A with x

the matrix of the linear system Bx = 0 whose rows are the basis vectors w₁, w₂ of W, so that its solution space is W⊥; a general matrix in the properties of the transpose, (A + B)ᵀ = Aᵀ + Bᵀ and (AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ
the transpose of the matrix B
a square matrix in the properties of the transpose: det(C) = det(Cᵀ) and, when C is invertible, (Cᵀ)⁻¹ = (C⁻¹)ᵀ
the transpose of the square matrix C
the inverse of the square matrix C, whose transpose (C⁻¹)ᵀ is the inverse of Cᵀ
the identity matrix, whose product with any vector x is Ix = x
the column space of a matrix A, the span of its columns, a subspace of ℝᵐ
the null space of a matrix A, the set of vectors x in ℝⁿ satisfying Ax = 0, a subspace of ℝⁿ
the rank of a matrix A, the number of pivot positions in A
the dimension of a subspace S, the number of vectors in any basis of S
the determinant of a square matrix A: for a 2 × 2 matrix, the area of the parallelogram formed by its columns, with the sign of their orientation
the set of all m-dimensional vectors
the vector whose entries are all zero
the dimension of a vector, the number of its components; the number of rows of an m × n matrix, which is the dimension of its columns and of the product Ax
the number of vectors v₁, v₂, …, vₙ in a linear combination, which is the number of columns of the matrix [v₁ v₂ … vₙ] and the dimension of a vector x it multiplies
the first vector of an orthogonal set w₁, w₂, …, wₙ, an orthogonal basis of the subspace W onto which b is projected; w₁ = [1, 2] in Preview Activity 6.3.1 and [2, 2, −1] in Activity 6.3.3
the second vector of the orthogonal set, w₂ = [−2, 1] in Preview Activity 6.3.1 and [1, 0, 2] in Activity 6.3.3
the third vector of the orthogonal set w₁, w₂, w₃ of Example 6.3.2, [1, −1, −2]
the last vector of the orthogonal set w₁, w₂, …, wₙ
a vector wᵢ of an orthogonal set, orthogonal to the others, whose weight in a linear combination b is cᵢ = (b·wᵢ)/(wᵢ·wᵢ)
the vector w = [2, 1] that defines the line L onto which b is projected, b̂ = (b·w)/(w·w) w; a nonzero vector scaled to the unit vector u = (1/|w|) w

a vector of ℝᵐ written as a linear combination of an orthogonal set, b = [7, 4] = 3w₁ − 2w₂; a vector not in the subspace W whose orthogonal projection onto W is sought, b = [2, 4] for the line L and b = [3, 9, 6] for the plane of Activity 6.3.3
the orthogonal projection of b onto a subspace W, the vector in W closest to b, characterized by b − b̂ being orthogonal to W
the vector b⊥ = b − b̂ in the orthogonal complement W⊥, the orthogonal projection of b onto W⊥, so that b = b̂ + b⊥
another vector on the line L, farther from b than b̂ is, since |b − y|² = |b − b̂|² + |b̂ − y|²
a unit vector, u = (1/|w|) w, parallel to w and of length 1; the orthonormal basis of a line
the first vector of an orthonormal set, u₁ = (1/√3)w₁ = [1/√3, −1/√3, 1/√3] in Activity 6.3.2, the first column of Q
the second vector of an orthonormal set, u₂ = [1/√2, 1/√2, 0] in Activity 6.3.2, the second column of Q
the third vector of an orthonormal set, u₃ = [1/√6, −1/√6, −2/√6] in Activity 6.3.2, the third column of Q
a vector uᵢ of an orthonormal set, orthogonal to the others and of unit length, so that uᵢ·uᵢ = 1 and the weight of uᵢ in the projection is b·uᵢ
the last vector of the orthonormal basis u₁, u₂, …, uₙ of W, the last column of Q
the weights c₁, c₂, …, cₙ of a linear combination of an orthogonal set, cᵢ = (b·wᵢ)/(wᵢ·wᵢ)
the scalar with b̂ = sw for the projection of b onto the line defined by w, found from (b − sw)·w = 0; a positive scalar with |sw| = s|w|

the matrix Q = [u₁ u₂ … uₙ] whose columns form an orthonormal set, so that QᵀQ = Iₙ and QQᵀ projects vectors onto the subspace spanned by its columns; when Q is square, its columns are an orthonormal basis of ℝᵐ and Q is called orthogonal, with Q⁻¹ = Qᵀ
the transpose of Q, whose product Qᵀb lists the dot products of the columns of Q with b, and which is the inverse of Q when Q is orthogonal
the inverse of an orthogonal matrix Q, which equals its transpose Qᵀ
the matrix P = QQᵀ that projects vectors orthogonally onto the subspace W spanned by the orthonormal columns of Q, with Col(P) = W and rank(P) = dim W
the identity matrix, whose product with any vector x is Ix = x
the n × n identity matrix, whose entries are zero except for the diagonal entries, all of which are 1
a subspace of ℝᵐ, such as a line or a plane through the origin, whose orthogonal complement W⊥ and orthogonal projections onto it are formed; W = Col(A) when its basis vectors are the columns of A
the orthogonal complement of W, the set of vectors in ℝᵐ each of which is orthogonal to every vector in W; a subspace with dim W⊥ = m − dim W, and Nul(Aᵀ) when W = Col(A)
a line through the origin, the set of scalar multiples of a vector, a 1-dimensional subspace
the orthogonal complement of the line L, the set of vectors orthogonal to every vector on L: a line in ℝ² or a plane in ℝ³
the column space of a matrix A, the span of its columns, a subspace of ℝᵐ
the null space of a matrix A, the set of vectors x in ℝⁿ satisfying Ax = 0, a subspace of ℝⁿ
the rank of a matrix A, the number of pivot positions in A
the span of a set of vectors, the set of all their linear combinations
the set of all m-dimensional vectors
the dimension of a vector, the number of its components; the number of rows of an m × n matrix, which is the dimension of its columns and of the product Ax
the number of vectors v₁, v₂, …, vₙ in a linear combination, which is the number of columns of the matrix [v₁ v₂ … vₙ] and the dimension of a vector x it multiplies
the first vector of a basis v₁, v₂, …, vₙ for the subspace W, not orthogonal, from which Gram-Schmidt builds the orthogonal basis, w₁ = v₁; the first column of A in the QR factorization
the second basis vector, whose orthogonal projection v̂₂ onto the line W₁ is subtracted to give w₂ = v₂ − v̂₂
the third basis vector, whose orthogonal projection v̂₃ onto the plane W₂ is subtracted to give w₃ = v₃ − v̂₃
the last vector of the basis v₁, v₂, …, vₙ of W, from which wₙ is formed by subtracting the projections onto w₁, …, wₙ₋₁
the orthogonal projection v̂₂ of v₂ onto W₁, the line defined by w₁
the orthogonal projection v̂₃ of v₃ onto W₂, the subspace spanned by w₁ and w₂
the first vector of the orthogonal basis produced by Gram-Schmidt, w₁ = v₁
the second vector of the orthogonal basis, w₂ = v₂ − (v₂·w₁)/(w₁·w₁) w₁, orthogonal to w₁
the third vector of the orthogonal basis, w₃ = v₃ − (v₃·w₁)/(w₁·w₁) w₁ − (v₃·w₂)/(w₂·w₂) w₂
the last vector of the orthogonal basis, vₙ minus its projections onto w₁, …, wₙ₋₁
the next-to-last vector wₙ₋₁ of the orthogonal basis, the last one whose projection is subtracted from vₙ
the jth vector of the orthogonal basis, scaled to the unit vector uⱼ = (1/|wⱼ|) wⱼ
the first vector of the orthonormal basis obtained by scaling w₁ to unit length, the first column of Q
the second vector of the orthonormal basis, w₂ scaled to unit length, the second column of Q
the third vector of the orthonormal basis, w₃ scaled to unit length, the third column of Q
the unit vector uⱼ = (1/|wⱼ|) wⱼ parallel to wⱼ, the jth column of Q
a subspace of ℝᵐ, such as a line or a plane through the origin, whose orthogonal complement W⊥ and orthogonal projections onto it are formed; W = Col(A) when its basis vectors are the columns of A
the line W₁ defined by w₁, the span of the first basis vector, onto which v₂ is projected
the two-dimensional subspace W₂ = Span{w₁, w₂} = Span{v₁, v₂}, onto which v₃ is projected
an m × n matrix A = [v₁ v₂ … vₙ] whose columns are linearly independent, factored as A = QR
the matrix Q of the QR factorization A = QR, whose columns form an orthonormal basis for Col(A), so that QᵀQ = I and QQᵀ projects onto Col(A)
the n × n upper triangular factor R of the QR factorization A = QR, whose jth column holds the weights writing the jth column of A as a combination of the first j columns of Q
the columns r₁, r₂, r₃ of R, with Qrⱼ = vⱼ, each holding the weights that write vⱼ as a combination of u₁, …, uⱼ (Activity 6.4.4)
the columns a₁, a₂, …, aₙ of A, whose dot products aᵢ·aⱼ are the entries of AᵀA = RᵀR (Exercise 6.4.8)
the transpose of Q, whose product Qᵀb lists the dot products of the columns of Q with b, and which is the inverse of Q when Q is orthogonal
the matrix P = QQᵀ that projects vectors orthogonally onto the subspace W spanned by the orthonormal columns of Q, with Col(P) = W and rank(P) = dim W
a vector whose orthogonal projection b̂ onto W or onto Col(A) is found with the orthonormal basis, b̂ = QQᵀb
the orthogonal projection of b onto a subspace W, the vector in W closest to b, characterized by b − b̂ being orthogonal to W
the solution of Ax = b̂, which is consistent since b̂ is in Col(A)
the weights c₁, c₂, …, cₙ of a linear combination of an orthogonal set, cᵢ = (b·wᵢ)/(wᵢ·wᵢ)
the column space of a matrix A, the span of its columns, a subspace of ℝᵐ
the span of a set of vectors, the set of all their linear combinations
the set of all m-dimensional vectors
the dimension of a vector, the number of its components; the number of rows of an m × n matrix, which is the dimension of its columns and of the product Ax
the number of vectors v₁, v₂, …, vₙ in a linear combination, which is the number of columns of the matrix [v₁ v₂ … vₙ] and the dimension of a vector x it multiplies

the matrix of the least-squares problem Ax = b: A = [1 x₁; 1 x₂; 1 x₃] for a line through the data points, the 15 × 2 matrix of ones and chirp rates, the 10 × 6 matrix of body measurements, the Vandermonde matrix of a polynomial fit; its columns are linearly independent and it factors as A = QR
the transpose of the m × n matrix A, the n × m matrix whose rows are the columns of A; the components of Aᵀx are the dot products of the columns of A with x
the right-hand side of the inconsistent system Ax = b, the vector of the data points' y-values, of temperatures or of BFI readings; not in Col(A), it is replaced by its orthogonal projection b̂
the orthogonal projection of b onto a subspace W, the vector in W closest to b, characterized by b − b̂ being orthogonal to W
the vector b⊥ = b − b̂ in the orthogonal complement W⊥, the orthogonal projection of b onto W⊥, so that b = b̂ + b⊥
the vector b̃ obtained by demeaning b, whose squared length |b̃|² normalizes |b − Ax̂|² in the coefficient of determination
the demeaned vector ṽ, obtained from v by subtracting the average of its components from each component
the unknown vector of Ax = b: x = [b; m] describing the line b + mx = y, or x = [β₀; β₁; …] of the parameters of the model

the least-squares approximate solution of Ax = b, the solution of Ax̂ = b̂, given by the normal equation AᵀAx̂ = Aᵀb or by x̂ = R⁻¹Qᵀb; x̂ = [−1/3, 1] for the three points of Activity 6.5.2 and [22.8, 3.4] for the crickets
the m-dimensional vector 1 all of whose entries are 1, a column of A in every model with a constant term, so that b·1 sums the components of b (Exercise 6.5.12)
the matrix Q of the QR factorization A = QR, whose columns form an orthonormal basis for Col(A), so that QᵀQ = I and QQᵀ projects onto Col(A)
the transpose of Q, whose product Qᵀb lists the dot products of the columns of Q with b, and which is the inverse of Q when Q is orthogonal
the n × n upper triangular factor R of the QR factorization A = QR, whose jth column holds the weights writing the jth column of A as a combination of the first j columns of Q
the inverse of the upper triangular factor R, computationally feasible since R is upper triangular, in x̂ = R⁻¹Qᵀb
the column space of a matrix A, the span of its columns, a subspace of ℝᵐ
the null space of a matrix A, the set of vectors x in ℝⁿ satisfying Ax = 0, a subspace of ℝⁿ
the vector whose entries are all zero
the horizontal coordinate of a data point (x, y), the input of the line b + mx = y or the polynomial β₀ + β₁x + β₂x² = y fit to the data
the vertical coordinate of a data point (x, y), the output of the line b + mx = y or the polynomial fit to the data
the horizontal coordinate xᵢ of the ith data point (xᵢ, yᵢ), an entry of the matrix A
the vertical coordinate yᵢ of the ith data point, a component of b; yᵢ − (b + mxᵢ) is the vertical distance from the point to the line
the y-intercept of the line b + mx = y, the first unknown of the least-squares problem of Activity 6.5.2
the slope of the line b + mx = y; also the number of rows of A, the number of data points
the constant term β₀ of the linear function or polynomial fit to the data, the first component of x̂
the coefficient β₁ of the first input variable, the chirp rate C or the weight, or of x in a polynomial
the coefficient β₂ of the second input variable or of x² in a polynomial
the coefficient β₃ of the third input variable or of x³ in a polynomial
the coefficient β₄ of the fourth input variable, the wrist circumference in the body fat model
the coefficient β₅ of the fifth input variable, the neck circumference in the body fat model
the chirp rate of a cricket in chirps per second, the input of the linear function β₀ + β₁C = T; also the constant C of the model P = CLʳ in Exercise 6.5.8
the outdoor temperature in degrees Fahrenheit, modeled by the linear function β₀ + β₁C = T
the coefficient of determination, R² = 1 − |b − Ax̂|²/|b̃|², between 0 and 1; the closer to 1, the better the fit: 0.75 for the three points, 0.69 for the crickets
the degree of the polynomial fit to the data, the degree of the Vandermonde matrix; a degree too high overfits the data
the number of vectors v₁, v₂, …, vₙ in a linear combination, which is the number of columns of the matrix [v₁ v₂ … vₙ] and the dimension of a vector x it multiplies
